## THE IDEA (one paragraph, no more)

The bridge is a lie. Every row of floating tiles has one safe landing: pick it, or fall into the sky. Knowledge is shared, so the room gets louder with every row.

## THIS GAME'S SPECIFICS

- IS IT A PARTY GAME? Yes, but only in this form: a group sharing one device, short loud turns, and reactions worth watching. A bridge where every column is a blind coin flip is a lottery, not a game - what makes it a party game is that the bridge STAYS REVEALED for the whole round, so each player learns from the ones who fell.
- Core loop: the group stands on the near cliff. The field is N columns wide (2-5, scaling with the round) and one row taller each time. On your turn you pick a column and hop: a solid tile thuds and you advance, a fake tile shatters, the screen shakes and you lose a life. That row's safe column is now known to everyone.
- TWO MODES IN ONE FILE (do not ship a second file): PARTY (2-6 players, 3 lives each, last one standing wins, rounds add columns and hazards - a tile that cracks on the SECOND landing is a great late-round twist) and SOLO (endless climb for the best row count). Solo has nobody to learn from, so its fake tiles carry a TELL that gets subtler as you climb: a faint seam, a missing rivet, a one-frame shimmer - solo is a perception game, party is memory and nerve. Same bridge generator, two skills.
- A mode toggle on the start screen costs one variable; a second file would duplicate about 70% of the code and the two copies would drift. This is recorded so it is not re-litigated.
- Juice: tile crack and shatter, a real fall (scale down + spin + the tile shrinking in perspective), wind streaks on a near-miss hop, screen shake on impact, a swelling heartbeat as the row count rises. Party mode gets one extra: whoever falls leaves a GHOST PLATE on that column, so the board visibly records the dead.
- Risks: the whole game is one decision repeated, so the tell system and the per-round twists must carry it, and a 6-player round must take about 90 seconds, not five.
- Full entry: FuturePlans/GAME_IDEAS.md section 6.18.

## HARD REQUIREMENTS (our shell stack - all mandatory)

1. ONE self-contained `.html`. All CSS, JS and art inline.
2. ZERO network calls at runtime: no CDNs, no external fonts, no analytics, no remote images.
   It must run perfectly from `file://` with the device offline.
3. Size budget: Tier 1 - see `CONTRACT.md` §2 (T1 <= 300 KB, T2 <= 450 KB, T3 <= 1 MB).
4. `STUDIO_GAME_MANIFEST` comment block with exactly these keys -
   `id / title / orientation / minPlayers / maxPlayers / aiSupport / online / tileColor / version`
   - values: `proposed: id cliff-rise / portrait / minPlayers 1 / maxPlayers 6 / aiSupport none / online false / tileColor #78909C / version 1`.
5. `window.Game` lifecycle with a simulation clock: `pause()`, `resume()`, `destroy()`.
   Pausing must freeze all timers, animation and audio; nothing may keep simulating in the
   background.
6. Studio SDK block, wrapped so the game runs fully when the native bridge is absent
   (browser test).
7. Ads ONLY through the shell bridge (banner + rewarded); a rewarded callback that arrives
   with no argument means GRANTED. If the device is offline, show a plain "check your
   internet connection" message - NEVER a simulated or fake ad.
8. Audio and vibration obey the shell settings (master sound, volume, vibration, haptic
   profile): no game sound may play when master sound is off. `Game.setSettings` receives
   `sound` / `haptics` / `volume` from the shell.
9. User-facing copy: plain text, no em dashes and no "--" anywhere in the UI.
10. Orientation portrait, with safe-area insets handled (notches, rounded corners).
11. Every inline `<script>` block must parse - verified with the syntax gate below.

## DO NOT

- Change the shell, add a second file, add a dependency, phone home, or invent gameplay
  beyond the idea above.
- Touch any file other than the target file (and, when the entry says so, the manifest
  block inside it).
- Launch the app or the game yourself. Build and install only; the director tests on device.
